title: Carlo Rovelli says fundamental physics is overrated
abstract:
Nature, Published online: 09 November 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03626-7

The theoretical physicist unpacks the need for more humility in science and whether artificial intelligence could ever become conscious.
headline: Renowned physicist argues science needs more humility, questions if AI can think.
why_it_matters: This is not a cancer research paper. It's a commentary by a theoretical physicist on the limits of fundamental physics and artificial intelligence. It does not directly address patient care or medical treatment.
key_findings: Physics may be overestimating its ability to explain everything about the universe
Scientists should be more humble about what they can and cannot know
The question of whether artificial intelligence could ever become conscious remains open and uncertain
There may be limits to what physics can tell us about reality
methods_snapshot: This is a perspective article and interview, not a research study with experimental methods. It represents the author's views and philosophical arguments about the scope and limitations of physics and AI.

glossary.definition: A scientist who uses math and logic to explain how the universe works, rather than doing hands-on experiments
The study of the most basic rules of nature, like gravity and the behavior of tiny particles
Computer systems designed to perform tasks that normally require human thinking
The state of being aware and able to think and feel — what makes you 'you'

limitations: This is a commentary piece, not original research. It presents philosophical arguments rather than experimental evidence, so it cannot make specific scientific claims that can be tested.
